newsitem.title: CANADA: BCE Bell unit maintains profit forecast.
newsitem.headline: BCE Bell unit maintains profit forecast.

text.p: BCE Inc unit Bell Canada expects to meet its profit forecast of C$850 million in 1997, despite increasing pricing pressures in the long-distance market, a senior official said on Friday.

"If we were going to be clearly off that target, I would be required to issue a notice to my investors that the target has in fact changed. We're not doing that," Bell Canada Chief Financial Officer Vincent Salvati told Reuters.
In late February, Bell lowered its 1997 profit target to C$850 million from C$950 million forecast earlier.
Salvati said Bell continued to face growing pricing pressures for long-distance services in Canada from big competitors such as Sprint Corp and AT&T Corp.

Bell's share of Canada's long-distance market has dropped by 33 per cent since the sector was deregulated in 1992 to allow competition. Salvati also expects Bell's share of the local telephone market to fall once its monopoly for those services ends in January 1.
"Price is going to become more and more a factor in buying behavior, especially in the residential market," he said.
Bell Canada operates Canada's largest telephone network, serving 7 million residential and commercial customers in Ontario and Quebec.
On Thursday, Bell told its employees that 2,200 more jobs would be cut under the company's three-year business transformation plan.
With the latest cuts, Bell expects to have reduced its workforce to 38,100 by 1998 from 51,500 at December 1994, exceding by 3,400 its original target of 10,000 job cuts under the plan.
Salvati said the cuts were an integral part of Bell's business plan for this year, but also key to its operating performance in 1998 and beyond.
BCE shares fell 0.70 to 42.25 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Friday on almost 1.8 million shares.
